subject: Mathematics

source.topic: Data handling: Collect, represent and interpret data
source.subtopic: Collect and sort data; represent data in a pictograph; represent sorted data

show.line: A picture graph! Each picture stands for one child. Four children like apples. Two children like bananas. Apples win!

rounds.prompt: Look at the graph. How many children like oranges? Count the pictures.
Which fruit do the most children like?
rounds.praise: Apples! The apple row is the longest.

rounds.prompt: Which fruit do the fewest children like?
This graph shows pets. How many children have a dog? Say the number.
Count the cats and the fish together on the pets graph. How many?
rounds.praise: Six! Four cats and two fish.

rounds.prompt: Sort the toys before we make a graph. Balls or cars?

hints: Each picture is one. Count the pictures in the row.
The longest row has the most.

beat_the_tutor.setup: My turn! I will read the fruit graph.
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! One, two, three, four. Four children like apples.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's count the apple pictures together. One, two, three, four!

parent_line: Can read a simple picture graph and say which has the most and the fewest.
